doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

chapter: Leading the Basie band and recordings
title: Leading the Basie Orchestra and the business side
summary: As leader he left booking and business to the Basie organization; Cecelia Foster handles his business now.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Did you enjoy your ten years almost directing the Basie Orchestra? Did you enjoy being in a position of leader, and the business end of things that must have been involved in that?

Well I enjoyed being the leader of the Basie Orchestra. I didn’t have to be bothered with the business end of things, I just collected a salary like everyone else. And I didn’t have to pay the guys off. One thing I had to deal with was people who came to me and said, “man, I need a raise, can you get me a raise?” And I dealt with the administration about that and it was either accepted or rejected.
So the Basie organization was a booking agent in itself?
And managed the day to day operations?

Right. I didn’t have to have anything to do with bookings or the business, and rightly so. Because as a businessman — that’s why Cecelia Foster does all my business. And whatever success I enjoy, thanks to her.
Well that’s a good pairing then.
Yes. We’ve got a beautiful partnership here.
Yeah. I can attest to the fact that she’s very professional by the way.
